title: Russ Morgan as leader, and Venuti and Rank in later years
summary: Morgan was a capable leader and arranger, Bill Challis became arranger, and Morehouse says Joe Venuti sounded the same over the years; Virginia met Bill Rank at festivals.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: The same thing. Okay. Can you remember anything about each, you know the kind of men that you were playing with? Can you describe like for example Russ Morgan? What kind of a leader was he?
Russ Morgan was a good leader. He was a good leader.
He was very capable.
Yeah. He knew where he was going.
Okay. Was he also doing the arrangements?
Yeah.
Were there other arrangers also?
No, he was doing most of the arranging.
Wasn't it Bill Challis who joined us. Bill Challis became their arranger.
Yeah he did later I think, Bill Challis. I don't have the year with me.
This is the original. There is my father here and my brother.
Oh yes, right. Here is a picture of your father and your brother together.
My father and my brother.
No, not yours. Jean Goldkette's Greystone orchestra in February, 1923.
Yes.
Uh huh. How about some of the others. Joe Venuti of course was playing violin back then. Did he sound - you heard Joe Venuti within recent years.
Oh sure.
Did he sound pretty much the same back in 1924 as he did 5 years ago?
Yeah.
He didn't change much.
No.
Okay. And you also heard Bill Rank I think, didn't you.
Bill Rank.
Have you heard Bill Rank in recent years, in a night club.
We heard him several times. We met him at different festivals.
The Bix festivals or others?
Yes.
